economy.summary: As House Appropriations Committee chair, said in response to the February 2026 state budget address that it is too expensive to live in Pennsylvania and that the governor had listened to everyday Pennsylvanians.
economy.short: Says it is too expensive to live in Pennsylvania.

taxes.summary: In a statement on House passage of the General Appropriations bill, said the budget returns money to working families and does not raise taxes while continuing investments in public education and public safety.
taxes.short: Says budget returns money to families without raising taxes.

abortion.summary: In a joint statement with House Democratic leadership responding to an April 2026 Commonwealth Court ruling, said the decision is a victory for women and families seeking health care and that House Democrats remain committed to protecting reproductive rights.
abortion.short: Called court ruling protecting reproductive rights a victory.

education.summary: His campaign says he advocates for increased public education funding, meeting the state's constitutional mandate for public schools, and sponsored the Pennsylvania Promise initiative to make higher education more affordable.
education.short: Advocates increased public education funding; sponsored Pennsylvania Promise.

energy.summary: Conservation Voters of Pennsylvania, which endorsed him in 2022, said he co-sponsored a bill to transition Pennsylvania to 100% renewable energy by 2050.
energy.short: Co-sponsored bill for 100% renewable energy by 2050.

guns.summary: His campaign highlights his work founding a Gun Violence Task Force and securing a $60 million grant for gun violence prevention efforts.
guns.short: Founded Gun Violence Task Force; secured gun-violence prevention grant.
